test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following local winds is known to bring rain to Tamil Nadu during winter?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Northeast monsoon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Northeast monsoon** is also known as the **retreating monsoon**. It is a significant weather phenomenon that brings substantial rainfall to the southeastern coast of India, particularly Tamil Nadu, during the **winter months of October to December**.
 
• The Northeast monsoon winds blow from the land to the sea, but they pick up moisture from the **Bay of Bengal** and bring rains to parts of Tamil Nadu. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• Tamil Nadu receives the majority of its annual rainfall (approximately **48%-60%**) from the Northeast monsoon during this period. This is in contrast to most of India, which receives rainfall during the Southwest monsoon.
 
• The other options (Jet Stream, Southwest Monsoon, and Nor'wester) are not responsible for rainfall in Tamil Nadu during the winter season. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Northeast Monsoon:**

 
 
• The Northeast monsoon typically occurs during **October to December**, after the Southwest monsoon withdraws. It is prominent along the **Coromandel Coast**, which includes Tamil Nadu and parts of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The winds are dry as they originate from the land; however, when they cross the **Bay of Bengal**, they pick up moisture and cause rainfall in southeastern India.
 
 
 
• **Jet Stream:**
 
 
• Jet streams are fast-moving air currents in the upper atmosphere, typically at an altitude of 10-15 km. They influence the movement of weather systems but are not directly responsible for rainfall during the winter in Tamil Nadu.
 
• They primarily affect the **onset and withdrawal of the monsoon** and are critical in shaping the **western disturbances** over northern India.
 
 
 
• **Southwest Monsoon:**
 
 
• The Southwest monsoon occurs from **June to September** and brings rainfall to most parts of India. However, Tamil Nadu lies in the rain shadow region of the Western Ghats, receiving limited rainfall during this season.
 
• Hence, the Southwest monsoon is not a significant contributor to Tamil Nadu's winter rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Nor'wester:**
 
 
• The Nor'wester is a localized thunderstorm phenomenon that occurs in northeastern India, particularly in the states of West Bengal, Assam, and Bihar, during the **pre-monsoon season** (March to May).
 
• It is not related to Tamil Nadu's winter rainfall.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Importance of Northeast Monsoon:**

 
 
• Tamil Nadu's agriculture heavily depends on the Northeast monsoon. Crops such as **rice, sugarcane, and millets** are cultivated during this period.
 
• The monsoon replenishes the state’s **water reservoirs** and is crucial for drinking water and irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Climate Variability:**
 
 
• Climate change and El Niño events can significantly impact the intensity and distribution of the Northeast monsoon rains.
 
• For instance, during **El Niño years**, Tamil Nadu may experience reduced rainfall, affecting agriculture and water availability.
